label: Dolbeault Theory
notes: This lecture spans printed pages 76 through 80. It is a bookkeeping lecture with real geometric payoff: an almost complex structure splits complexified tangent spaces into two eigenspaces, forms acquire a type, and the exterior derivative breaks into partial and dbar pieces that organize holomorphic data into one bigraded picture.

label: Complexifying the Tangent Space
notes: We tensor the real tangent space with the complex numbers so that the operator J, which squares to minus the identity, can be diagonalized. Over the reals J has no eigenvalues; over the complexification it gains the eigenvalues plus i and minus i, and those eigenspaces are the whole story.

label: The Eigenspace Splitting
notes: The projections P10 and P01 are built directly from J as one half of the identity minus or plus i times J. They are complementary idempotents whose images are the plus i and minus i eigenspaces. Emphasize that this splitting is pointwise linear algebra valid for any almost complex structure.

label: Dual Splitting of One-Forms
notes: Dualizing the tangent splitting gives the cotangent decomposition into the one-zero and zero-one parts. A complex-valued one-form is the sum of a holomorphic-type and an antiholomorphic-type piece. In a complex chart these are spanned by the differentials of the coordinates and their conjugates.

label: Forms of Type (p,q)
notes: Taking wedge powers extends the splitting to all degrees. A form of type p,q has p holomorphic legs and q antiholomorphic legs, and the complex k-forms decompose as the direct sum over p plus q equal to k. This bigrading is the coordinate system for everything that follows.

label: The Bigraded Diamond
notes: Lay the type spaces out on a grid indexed by p horizontally and q vertically. This is the Hodge diamond picture. Every operator we meet will be read as an arrow on this grid, so getting students comfortable moving between a node and its neighbors pays off immediately.

label: Splitting the Exterior Derivative
notes: Apply d to a p,q form and project the result onto each type component. In general d lands in four neighboring boxes, but two of them vanish exactly when the structure is integrable. The surviving pieces are partial, raising p, and dbar, raising q.

label: The Dolbeault Operators
notes: Define partial as the type p plus one, q component of d and dbar as the type p, q plus one component. In the integrable case d equals partial plus dbar with no extra terms. On the grid partial moves east and dbar moves south, exactly as the lattice figure shows.

label: J-Holomorphic Functions
notes: On functions the test is small and powerful. A function is J-holomorphic precisely when dbar f vanishes, which in a chart is the Cauchy-Riemann condition. The symbolic checks confirm that polynomials in z are killed by dbar while polynomials in z-bar are killed by partial.

label: The Dolbeault Complex
notes: Expanding d squared equals zero by type, and using that the cross terms vanish under integrability, forces dbar squared to equal zero. That makes each row of the diamond a cochain complex. Its cohomology is the Dolbeault cohomology, the bigraded refinement of de Rham cohomology.

label: Nijenhuis and Newlander-Nirenberg
notes: The clean two-term splitting is not automatic. The Nijenhuis tensor measures the failure of the one-zero distribution to be closed under bracket, and it is the precise obstruction. Newlander-Nirenberg says its vanishing is equivalent to the existence of holomorphic charts making J integrable.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: Recap the pipeline: complexify, split into eigenspaces, grade forms by type, project d into partial and dbar, and read holomorphicity as dbar f equals zero. Dolbeault cohomology lives on the diamond when integrability holds. The next lecture takes up the integrability tests this obstruction opens.
